references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the ram of consecration (אֵיל הַמִּלֻּאִים) is mentioned as being used in the priestly ordination.
Parallel account of the ram of consecration that was to be cooked and eaten in a holy place by Aaron and his sons.
Regulation stating that the sin offering must be eaten in a holy place, following the same principle as applies to the ram of consecration.
Regulations concerning peace offerings that were to be eaten on the same day, with similar rules for holy meals.
Continuation of the text explaining that Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The Nazirite offering, which also involved cooking the ram in a holy place.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes regulations about cooking sacrifices in a holy place.
Both are parts of the same ordination ritual (Exodus 29) and describe successive steps in the handling of the sacrificial animal.
Lev 10:13 confirms and expands on the requirement to consume the sacrificial meat in a holy place as given in Ex 29:31.
Both verses state that the consumption of holy offerings must take place in a specific holy location.
Both verses describe different parts of the same ordination ritual (Ex 29/Lv 8): what is eaten and what remains to be burned.
